blogs.title: How LLMs Can Become Your Personal Feature Engineer for Tabular Data
blogs.description: Delve into the core idea of FeatLLM: using a large language model to automatically craft binary features (rules) from raw tabular columns, eliminating the need for end‑to‑end LLM inference and cutting inference latency.

blogs.title: From Raw Numbers to Pruned Rules: The Two‑Step Reasoning Behind FeatLLM
blogs.description: Explore how FeatLLM’s prompt is structured into (1) prior‑knowledge reasoning about feature–label relationships and (2) data‑driven rule extraction, mirroring an expert’s diagnosis process and boosting few‑shot performance.

blogs.title: Rule‑Based Features vs. Heavy‑Weight Models: Why Simplicity Wins in Low‑Shot Scenarios
blogs.description: Compare FeatLLM’s lightweight linear classifier operating on LLM‑generated rules with traditional tree or XGBoost models, highlighting why fewer parameters and rule sparsity help when labels are scarce.

blogs.title: Ensembling by Bagging Rules: Making LLMs Robust to Noise and Prompt Size Limits
blogs.description: Explain how repeatedly sampling small subsets of data/columns and generating diverse rule sets allows FeatLLM to sidestep prompt length constraints and mitigate spurious correlations—essential for real‑world tabular datasets.

blogs.title: Benchmarks that Matter: FeatLLM vs. State‑of‑the‑Art on 13 Diverse Tabular Tasks
blogs.description: Summarize the experimental results showing FeatLLM outperforming or matching baselines across medical, finance, synthetic, and newly released datasets, even with as few as 4 labeled examples.

blogs.title: Practical Trade‑Offs: Training Time, Inference Speed and API Costs for FeatLLM
blogs.description: Break down the runtime profile of FeatLLM compared to other LLM‑based tabular methods—showing its competitive inference speed and modest number of API calls, making it viable for production systems.

blogs.title: What do the Rules Really Tell You? Insights from Feature Quality Analysis
blogs.description: Discuss the study measuring AUROC of individual rule‐based features, illustrating how FeatLLM tends to discover informative conditions while discarding noisy ones during weight tuning.

blogs.title: Future Directions: Going Beyond Binary Rules and Scaling to Large Datasets
blogs.description: Speculate on extending FeatLLM to higher–cardinality or numerical feature transformations, integrating multi–class rules, and ensuring interpretability while handling larger data volumes.
